payload.roles:
- The adjudicating owner, away from the desk: reads the brief and taps; the only party who can close the loop.
- The same owner as custodian of the material: their ledger content is what travels, and their topic and token are the credentials.
- The driving agent: parks on the gate, must know whether the offer actually reached anyone.
- The relay (ntfy): carries the card and the answer; retains for about twelve hours; authenticates nobody.
- The static host (Workers KV): stores and serves the page; must be able to learn nothing from it.
- The phone's ntfy app: renders the card and fires the action - the component nobody can test by assertion, only by tapping.
- The maintainer of the account: the owner in another hat, holding a free-tier worker, namespace and token that no code owns.
payload.tensions:
T1 - the adjudicating owner versus the custodian owner. Deciding well wants the brief rich and complete; protecting the material wants as little as possible to leave the machine. RESOLUTION: the content leaves encrypted rather than trimmed, so richness costs secrecy nothing at the host - and the pressure test corrected the claim: the topic still exposes it to whoever holds the topic, which is the accepted risk already ruled.

T2 - the owner versus the agent. The owner wants nothing buzzing during an unattended run; the agent must not park on a gate the owner never saw. RESOLUTION: publish is decided by WHO ADJUDICATES, not by whether a lane happens to be running - self-blessed gates stay silent, human-blessed gates always publish.

T3 - the relay versus the host. The card must stay a pointer (short, and cached by a third party), while the decision needs a page (long, and worth protecting). RESOLUTION: split them - the message carries no content, only a link whose fragment carries the key.

T4 - the phone app versus everyone. It is the one component that cannot be mocked, and every previous attempt trusted it on documentation. RESOLUTION: acceptance is a tap on a real device, and this iteration's own release gate is that tap.

T5 - the account maintainer versus the adjudicating owner. A free-tier host that no code owns will eventually lapse, while the owner expects the brief to be there. RESOLUTION: the ladder degrades - actions alone still decide the gate - provided the degradation is reported rather than silent, which is why reporting is a requirement and not a nicety.
